title: Permit application
description: One application for a building, trade, land-use, right-of-way or other local-government permit, followed from submission through intake, plan review by discipline and cycle, fees, the statutory review clock, the decision and inspections. Fields that correspond to the Building and Land Development Specification (BLDS), an open data specification for publishing permit data, are mapped in the docs, so a jurisdiction can publish BLDS data from these records. The format follows common local-government practice; it doesn't encode any jurisdiction's code or deadlines.

$schema.title: Schema
$schema.description: The `$id` of the schema the record follows, so a reader can tell what the record is without guessing. Optional; recordType and schemaVersion say the same thing.

recordType.title: Record type
recordType.description: Always permit-application. Lets a reader (or validate()) tell the format apart from the others in this repository.

schemaVersion.title: Schema version
schemaVersion.description: The version of this format the record follows. Each version of the schema accepts only its own version string, so a record never silently passes against a schema it wasn't written for.

id.description: This application's identifier, unique within the system that created it. Often the application or case number; the permit number, once issued, is decision.permitNumber (they may be the same).

externalIds.title: External identifiers
externalIds.description: Ids for this application in other systems, such as the jurisdiction's permitting system when the record comes from a contractor's or applicant's software, or a state or regional portal.

updatedAt.description: When the record was last changed.

jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction whose permit is sought, and the department that issues it.

permitType.title: Permit type
permitType.description: What kind of permit is sought.

category.title: Category
category.description: The broad kind of permit: building; demolition; electrical; mechanical; plumbing; fire (fire alarm, sprinkler, fire code operational permits); grading (grading, excavation, stormwater); right-of-way (street use, driveway, skip or dumpster, utility work in the street); sign; zoning (zoning clearance, variance); land-use (subdivision, site plan, conditional use); environmental; special-event; or other. The first several match BLDS PermitTypeMapped values (Building, Demolition, Electrical, Mechanical, Plumbing, Grading); BLDS's Roof, Fence and Pool/Spa are building permits here, with the specific type in subtype.

subtype.title: Subtype
subtype.description: The jurisdiction's own name for the permit type, as it appears on the application and the permit. This is BLDS PermitType or PermitTypeDesc.

workClass.title: Work class
workClass.description: What the work does to the structure: new (new construction); addition; alteration (remodel or tenant improvement); repair (including replacement in kind); demolition; change-of-use (a new occupancy for an existing building); or other. For BLDS WorkClassMapped, new maps to New and the others to Existing.

residential.title: Residential
residential.description: Whether the work is to a residential building (true) or not (false). Jurisdictions draw this line differently; BLDS PermitClassMapped uses Residential for single-family and duplex only and puts multifamily with commercial, so check the building type before mapping.

description.title: Description of work
description.description: What the applicant proposes to do, in the applicant's or the jurisdiction's words. This is what appears on the permit and in published permit data (BLDS Description), so write it to be read by the public.
examples: Single-story 420 sq ft rear addition with new bathroom; relocate water heater.

valuation.description: The declared value of the work (BLDS EstProjectCost). Many jurisdictions compute fees from it.

applicant.description: Who is applying. Give their role too, since the applicant may be the owner, the contractor or an agent.

parties.title: Other parties
parties.description: Owners, contractors, design professionals, agents and tenants on the application besides the applicant.

site.title: Site
site.description: Where the work will happen. Give at least one of a parcel number, an address or coordinates; right-of-way work often has an address or coordinates but no parcel.

parcelNumber.title: Parcel number
parcelNumber.description: The identifier of the land parcel used for tax assessment: the assessor's parcel number (APN), parcel identification number (PIN), tax id or equivalent (BLDS PIN). Written as the assessor writes it.

address.description: The site's street address (BLDS OriginalAddress1, OriginalCity, OriginalState, OriginalZip).

location.description: The site's coordinates (BLDS Latitude and Longitude), for mapping and for sites without an address.

zoning.title: Zoning
zoning.description: The parcel's zoning designation, as the jurisdiction writes it.

floodZone.title: Flood zone
floodZone.description: The flood hazard zone, if the site is mapped, as shown on the flood map (in the US, the FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map zone).

historicDistrict.title: Historic district
historicDistrict.description: Whether the site is in a designated historic district, which usually adds a historic preservation review.

building.title: Building
building.description: Facts about the building or structure, for building permits. Leave out for permits that don't involve a building.

occupancyGroup.title: Occupancy group
occupancyGroup.description: The building code occupancy classification, as the adopted code writes it (in the International Building Code, for example R-3 for one- and two-family dwellings or B for business).

constructionType.title: Construction type
constructionType.description: The building code construction type, as the adopted code writes it.

stories.title: Stories
stories.description: Number of stories above grade plane after the work.

dwellingUnits.title: Dwelling units
dwellingUnits.description: Net dwelling units added by the work: positive when units are added, negative when removed, 0 when unchanged. BLDS HousingUnits is the total units in the building, which is a different number.

area.title: Area
area.description: Floor area affected by the work, with its unit. BLDS TotalSqFt is in square feet; convert square metres before publishing.

submittedAt.description: When the application was submitted (BLDS AppliedDate is the date part, in the jurisdiction's time zone).

documents.title: Submitted documents
documents.description: Plans and documents submitted with the application. Each points at a file in attachments; a resubmitted plan set is a new entry with a new revision.

attachmentId.description: The id of the file in the record's attachments. The validator checks it exists.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: site-plan; architectural-plans; structural-calculations; energy-compliance (energy code forms or calculations); mechanical-electrical-plumbing-plans; survey; photographs; owner-authorization (owner's consent for an agent or contractor to apply); contractor-license; insurance-certificate; environmental-review; or other.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: Revision number or label, as written on the plans.

fees.title: Fees
fees.description: Fees assessed on the application, one line per fee. BLDS Fee is a single total; sum the lines when publishing.

code.title: Code
code.description: The jurisdiction's fee code from its fee schedule.

amount.description: The fee amount. Use a negative amount for a credit line.

status.title: Status
status.description: assessed (calculated, not yet billed); invoiced; paid; waived; or refunded.

receipt.title: Receipt
receipt.description: The receipt or payment transaction reference.

reviews.title: Plan reviews
reviews.description: Plan reviews by each discipline, one entry per discipline per review cycle, so the record shows how many rounds of corrections each discipline required.

items.title: Plan review
items.description: One discipline's review in one cycle.

discipline.title: Discipline
discipline.description: The reviewing discipline: zoning; building; structural; fire; electrical; mechanical; plumbing; civil-engineering; environmental; health (environmental health, food service); historic-preservation; transportation; utilities; or other.

cycle.title: Cycle
cycle.description: The review cycle, starting at 1. Each resubmission in response to corrections starts a new cycle.

reviewer.description: Who reviewed (a plans examiner, planner or engineer).

completedAt.description: When it was completed. Must not be before startedAt.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: approved; approved-with-conditions; corrections-required (the applicant must revise and resubmit); denied; or not-applicable (the discipline found nothing to review).

comments.title: Comments
comments.description: Review comments the applicant must address.

text.title: Text
text.description: The comment, as written to the applicant.

sheet.title: Sheet
sheet.description: The plan sheet the comment refers to.

codeSection.title: Code section
codeSection.description: The code section cited, as the adopted code numbers it.

resolved.title: Resolved
resolved.description: Whether the comment has been resolved in a later submission.

statutoryClock.title: Statutory review clock
statutoryClock.description: The time limit a law, ordinance or policy sets for deciding the application, and the state of the clock. Many jurisdictions have such limits (and some deem a permit approved if the limit passes), with different rules for when the clock starts, which days count and what pauses it. The record states the basis and the counting it applied; it does not compute deadlines. startedAt and pauses are instants with a UTC offset; days are counted in timeZone's calendar, and dueOn is a date in that zone.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: The law, ordinance or policy that sets the deadline, cited as the jurisdiction cites it.

days.title: Days allowed
days.description: Days allowed for the decision under the basis.

dayType.title: Day type
dayType.description: Whether the days are calendar or business days.

timeZone.title: Time zone
timeZone.description: The IANA time zone whose calendar the jurisdiction counts days in. dueOn is a date in this zone, so every system computes the same day for a deadline near midnight. Required whenever dueOn is given.

startedAt.description: When the clock started (often when the application was deemed complete, not when it was submitted).

dueOn.description: The date, in timeZone, by which the decision is due under the basis, after pauses.

pauses.title: Pauses
pauses.description: Periods when the clock stopped, for example while waiting for the applicant to respond to corrections.

items.title: Pause
items.description: One period when the clock stopped.

to.description: When the pause ended; leave out while it continues. Must not be before from.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: awaiting-applicant (corrections or information requested); fees-outstanding; applicant-request (the applicant asked for more time); third-party-review (an outside agency's review that the basis allows to pause the clock); or other.

consequenceIfMissed.title: Consequence if missed
consequenceIfMissed.description: What the basis says happens when the deadline passes: deemed-approved; fee-refund; escalation (to a supervisor or another body); none; or unspecified (the basis doesn't say, or nobody has checked).

inspections.title: Inspections
inspections.description: Inspections of the permitted work, one entry per inspection visit (a failed inspection followed by a re-inspection is two entries).

type.title: Type
type.description: The inspection, as the jurisdiction names it on the permit card.

requestedFor.description: The date the inspection was requested for.

result.title: Result
result.description: scheduled (not yet done); passed; failed (correction and re-inspection needed); partial (part of the work approved); cancelled; or no-access (the inspector couldn't get to the work).

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: The inspector's notes and any corrections required.

decision.title: Decision
decision.description: The jurisdiction's decision on the application. An issued permit's number, conditions and expiry are here.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: issued (the permit is issued; permitNumber is required); approved (approved but not yet issued, for example while fees are unpaid); denied; withdrawn (by the applicant); expired (the application lapsed, or the issued permit expired before final); or revoked.

decidedAt.description: When the decision was made. For an issued permit, BLDS IssuedDate is the date part in the jurisdiction's time zone.

decidedBy.description: Who decided, usually by title (Building Official, Planning Director).

permitNumber.title: Permit number
permitNumber.description: The number of the issued permit (BLDS PermitNum). Required when the outcome is issued.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.description: Conditions of approval, each as stated on the permit.

reasons.title: Reasons
reasons.description: Reasons for a denial or revocation, as given to the applicant. Usually needed for an appeal.

expiresOn.description: When the permit (or the approval) expires if work doesn't start or progress (BLDS ExpiresDate). Must not be before the decision.

appealDeadline.description: The last day to file an appeal of the decision.

status.description: Where the application is: draft (not yet submitted); submitted; intake-review (checking completeness); incomplete (the applicant must supply more); in-review (plan review); corrections-required; approved; issued; under-inspection; finaled (all inspections passed and the permit closed); denied; withdrawn; expired; or revoked. The docs map these to BLDS StatusCurrentMapped.

statusHistory.title: Status history
statusHistory.description: Every status the application has had, oldest first, ending at the current status (the validator checks both). BLDS CompletedDate is the date of the finaled entry.

status.description: The status the record moved to, one of this format's status values.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Files that belong to the application: plans, calculations, photographs, letters. Plans submitted to a public agency are often public records, but may still contain personal data or security-sensitive details; set classification accordingly.

auditTrail.title: Audit trail
auditTrail.description: Recorded actions on the application, oldest first.

extensions.description: Local fields this format doesn't define, namespaced as <namespace>:<field>, for example examplecity:councilDistrict.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status values of this format, defined once so status and statusHistory use the same list. Where the application is: draft (not yet submitted); submitted; intake-review (checking completeness); incomplete (the applicant must supply more); in-review (plan review); corrections-required; approved; issued; under-inspection; finaled (all inspections passed and the permit closed); denied; withdrawn; expired; or revoked. The docs map these to BLDS StatusCurrentMapped.

party.title: Party
party.description: A person or organization on the application, in a role. Give a person, an organization, or both (a named contact at a firm). Names and mailing addresses of individuals, such as homeowners, are personal data even where permit records are public.

role.title: Role
role.description: owner (the property owner); applicant (where the applicant has no other role); contractor; architect; engineer; agent (a permit expediter or other representative); tenant; or other.

organization.description: The organization (BLDS ContractorCompanyName, for a contractor).

mailingAddress.description: Where to send notices to the party, when it differs from the site.

license.title: License
license.description: A professional or contractor license the party holds, which many jurisdictions verify before issuing a permit.

number.title: Number
number.description: The license number (BLDS ContractorLicNum, for a contractor).

issuer.title: Issuer
issuer.description: The licensing board or agency (BLDS ContractorStateLic records the licensing state).
